physical_skill: Two-handed carry of a free-standing 30x15x0.8 cm, 0.75 kg ceramic tile balanced on its long edge (falls past about 3 degrees of tilt), set down upright in a 4.5 cm slot behind a toe strip, then a controlled tip-back onto two posts with a loosened caging grip, releasing only once its weight is on the posts and moving the hands 3 cm clear.
valid_shortcuts: One arm is allowed: a one-arm off-centre pinch scored 0.5 (leaning on both posts, short of the 1.0 placement); a one-arm route that meets every 1.0 condition would rightly score 1.0.
Tipping the tile back onto the posts without the toe strip slot (from in front of the strip) scores 0.5, not 1.0.
Grippers left around the leaning tile score 0 (hands-clear test, fingertips within 3 cm); pushing the standing tile's top makes it fall and scores 0; doing nothing scores 0.
A fall is latched and cleared only in the reset hook, so standing the tile back up after a fall cannot recover credit.
queries: refresh 19 Nov: PRs above 2560 grepped for upright|stand|lean|plate|frame|board|panel|sheet|pane|glass|mirror|tray|propped|against

nearest_prs.comparison: Unracks panels from a leaning rack, standing each upright on a mat with a tilt limit; the skill is choosing and removing panels that lean on the target. Ours carries a free-standing tile into a rack and transfers it from balanced-upright to leaning; the reverse transfer with a release-timing difficulty.

Glass pane lifted from a sash with suction lifters and laid flat on bearers; tool operation (lever lock) and flat placement. Ours has no tool and the difficulty is the unstable on-edge balance through the carry and the lean-back release.
A tipped case leans on a locker door; opening the door while controlling the case. Shares controlling a leaning object, but the object, mechanism (door) and goal differ.
Tall canister leaned under a low shelf then stood up; inverse direction (lean then upright) and clearance-driven. Ours ends in a lean on supports and is about release under marginal stability.

Small acrylic offcuts in a rack re-chocked with one prop block: support handover sequencing on a deliberately unstable strip. Ours is a real-scale tile with real mass, no built-in instability (a tile on its edge is naturally marginal), and the skill is carry and lean-back release, not chock handover.
Press a leaning row of books upright and hold it while inserting a book; hold-one-while-working skill. Ours has no insertion and ends with the object deliberately leaning.

Hang a framed picture on a wall hook by its wire, level, then let go: a hanging/hook-engagement skill on a vertical wall. Ours carries an edge-balanced tile into a floor slot and transfers it from upright to leaning on two posts; no hook, wire or levelling.

distinct_from_nearest: No accepted or pending task on the refreshed board carries a sheet or tile that stands balanced on its edge into a lean rack and releases it only after it leans. Own held folder chock-leaning-panel-in-floor-channel (not submitted at check time) stands a fallen panel up in a channel and secures it with a chock: different end state and mechanism. Weakness noted: importance rests on everyday relatability of leaning flat objects, not an occupation or injury hazard. Refreshed 19 Nov: no new pending or accepted task with an edge-standing tile/sheet carried into a lean rack; own chock-leaning-panel-in-floor-channel has not been submitted.
